stance.label: Taiwan back in a bear market; stick to the regular plan

headline: Foreign investors dump NT$123.6B; TAIEX falls 1,926 points, back below the bear line in one day
summary: Taiwan's rebound lasted one day: foreign investors sold for an 8th day and Trump talked up chip tariffs, so the TAIEX closed below the bear-market line. By the rules Taiwan is back to "bear, risk rising", but the credit and economy lights are still off, so this is not an economy-driven bear yet. Keep regular investing on plan; tonight watch PCE and the Section 301 tariff rates.

watch.label: TAIEX bear line (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 38,195.43 on 11/25, about 4% below; must reclaim it and hold the 200-day line for 5 days to go back to a pullback

watch.label: 0050 tier 5 (−30% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 90.30 on 11/25, 9.7% away; the nearest tier among the Taiwan-linked tracked names

watch.label: QQQ tier 4 (−20% from peak)
watch.note: Closed 638.10 on 11/24, 4.8% away; the nearest tier of all nine

overview.lead: Taiwan gave back almost all of the prior day's rebound, and it was foreign selling hitting the heavyweights. This is a flows-plus-policy hit, not simple profit-taking.
points: The TAIEX fell 4.8% to 38,195, back below the bear line.
It was down about 3,440 points at one point before trimming losses late.
Foreign investors sold NT$123.6B, the 7th-largest ever, and have sold for eight straight sessions.
Trump said tariffs on imported chips could reach 200% in two years, and named Taiwan.
The US is still a pullback: only 1 S&P 500 systemic light is on.

focus.lead: The three Taiwan names took the worst hit today, but the two Taiwan fund NAVs only run to 11/24, so the next NAV will show today's drop all at once.
points: 0050 fell 5.64%; tier 5 is 9.7% away, the nearest tier among the Taiwan-linked names.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) jumped on 11/24 NAVs and will give it back.
The two Taiwan funds share 6 of their top ten, about 27% weight; Global Unichip (3443) hit limit-down today.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV is still at 11/20.
QQQ is 4.8% from tier 4, still the nearest of all nine.

position.lead: No new trigger by the framework today, but 0050's gap to tier 5 shrank from nearly 15% to under 10%.
points: 0050 has used 70% of its reserve; tier 5 is 9.7% away.
QQQ has used 45% of its reserve; tier 4 is 4.8% away.
SPY tier 3 is 7.9% away; AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) is 8.3% away.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan tier 5 is 6.7% away (11/20 NAV).
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) tier 5 is 9.3% away (11/24 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology (LU0060230025) have used all tiers.

macro.lead: Both pressures on Taiwan are on today: US rate-hike expectations have not eased, and tariffs moved from a capacity probe to chips, with Taiwan named.
points: Trump said on 11/24 that chip tariffs would be 200% in two years; no details yet.
The Section 301 excess-capacity probe covers Taiwan; new tariffs could come this week, rates unknown.
The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91%, and December hike odds stay high.
The high-yield spread is 3.63% (11/23), far from the 5% warning line.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan sentiment is washed out, but not at capitulation: margin debt is down over a quarter in a month, and only a tenth of stocks are above the 200-day line.
points: Only 10% of Taiwan stocks are above the 200-day line, 5% above the 50-day line.
1 new high, 87 new lows.
Margin debt is down 27.3% in 20 days; the deleveraging signal is on.
The CNN Fear & Greed Index is 17.4, still extreme fear.

sectors.lead: No safe place today: tech led the drop, financials fell hard too, and only food was flat.
points: Electronics distribution fell 6.65%; electronic components are down 33% in a month.
Financials slumped; Hua Nan Financial (2880) and SinoPac Financial (2890) hit limit-down.
Food rose 0.07%, the only major sector in the green.
About 100 stocks hit limit-down; only 106 closed higher.

taiwan.lead: Foreign money is really leaving: 8 days of cash selling, futures net shorts above 105,000 contracts, and big local fund buying only absorbed part of it.
points: Foreign investors sold NT$123.66B, about NT$1.2T over the past month.
Local investment trusts bought NT$53.5B; the three institutional groups sold NT$83.0B net.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures are 105,709 contracts, up 6,271 in five days.
TSMC (2330) fell 3.59% to NT$2,150; MediaTek (2454) hit limit-down.
Hon Hai (2317) fell 8.83%; ASE Technology (3711) fell 7.92%.
Margin debt rose NT$19.7B on the 11/24 rebound; today's drop may force another round of margin calls.

watch.lead: Two things for US stocks tonight: whether PCE makes a hike more certain, and the Section 301 tariff rate for Taiwan.
points: 11/25 21:30 Taipei: US October PCE and Q3 GDP revision.
New Section 301 tariffs could come this week; Taiwan's rate is key for Taiwan stocks tomorrow.
US markets close 11/26 for Thanksgiving and close early 11/27; volume will be thin.
12/1: Jensen Huang faces a closed-door House committee session.
Whether the TAIEX reclaims 39,858 decides if it leaves bear territory.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is back to "bear, risk rising" and the US is still a pullback. Taiwan's two lights are breadth and global risk appetite; the credit and economy lights are still off.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 8.3% below the 200-day line for 8 days, but the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: 2 on for Taiwan (S&P 500 below its 200-day line, breadth collapse), 1 on for the US.
Credit, the economy and financial conditions are all fine; the high-yield spread is 3.63%, far from 5%.
Bottoming signals: 2 on for Taiwan, margin debt down 27.3% in 20 days and a breadth washout; oversold and extreme foreign selling are not on.
From here, Taiwan usually fell further: all 9 cases since 2000 broke −20%, and 4 of them broke −30%.
Only 1 case was as fast as this one; the sample is too small, use it only as a reference.
Flip: close back above 39,858, then hold 41,628 for five days, and it goes back to a pullback.
3+ systemic lights, or the 200-day line going flat (now +2.73%), would mean a full bear trend.

news.title: TAIEX plunged 1,926 points, or 4.8%, to 38,195; it was down about 3,440 points intraday
news.read: The prior day's rebound was gone in one day and the close is back below the bear line; 0050 and the two Taiwan funds take the brunt.

news.title: Foreign investors sold NT$123.65B, the 7th-largest ever; investment trusts bought NT$53.5B
news.read: Eight days of foreign selling that local institutions cannot fully absorb; flows will not stabilize until foreigners turn buyers.

news.title: About 100 stocks hit limit-down; foreign net short futures rose to 105,709 contracts
news.read: Futures shorts keep growing; foreign hedging on Taiwan has not eased.

news.title: Trump said Taiwan took the US chip market and imported chips will face 200% tariffs in two years
news.read: It is a verbal claim without details, but it hits TSMC and Taiwan tech heavyweights directly and set off today's selling.

news.title: The US is preparing Section 301 tariffs on 16 economies including Taiwan; could come this week, rates unknown
news.read: Reports cite a 15% cap for the EU, Japan and Korea but nothing for Taiwan; until rates are out, it is an overhang for Taiwan and Japan.

news.title: Dell AI server revenue was $22B, up 291%; full-year guidance raised to $78B
news.read: AI demand has not weakened; this drop is policy and flows, and demand supports Taiwan's server supply chain over time.

news.title: Nvidia fell about 6%; Micron and SK Hynix fell nearly 10%
news.read: US chips gave back gains overnight first, and Taiwan tech heavyweights caught up today.

events.label: US October PCE, Q3 GDP revision (21:30 Taipei)
New US Section 301 excess-capacity tariffs could come this week (16 economies incl. Taiwan)

actions.head: Keep regular investing on plan.

actions.head: Do not change the plan over one 4.8% drop.
actions.text: The call is bear, but the credit and economy lights are off; the rules have not changed, so actions need not either.

actions.head: Watch for foreign selling to stop and tonight's tariff rates.
actions.text: Foreign buying and a TAIEX close back above 39,858 would signal flows stabilizing.

actions.head: 3+ systemic lights would turn Taiwan into an economy- or credit-driven bear.
actions.text: 2 are on now; a flat 200-day line would also change the call.
